releases.body:
## `better-auth`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed `/admin/create-user` leaving a user without a credential account when creating that account failed, such as a database hook throwing, which made retrying with the same email fail with `USER_ALREADY_EXISTS_USE_ANOTHER_EMAIL` ([#12338](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12338))
- Fixed `/admin/create-user` leaving a user without a credential account when the password was rejected, such as by the Have I Been Pwned plugin, which made retrying with the same email fail with `USER_ALREADY_EXISTS_USE_ANOTHER_EMAIL` ([#12335](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12335))
- Fixed client actions ignoring the HTTP method passed in second-argument fetch options, and attaching a request body when the method was a lowercase `get` or `HEAD` ([#12336](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12336))
- Fixed plugin schema overrides (`modelName` and field names) leaking into other instances of the same plugin in one process ([#12319](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12319))
- Fixed `/device/token` returning `invalid_grant` instead of `invalid_client` when `validateClient` rejects the `client_id`, matching `/device/code` and RFC 6749 section 5.2 ([#12246](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12246))
- Fixed OAuth sign-in failing with `state_mismatch` during the daylight saving time fall-back hour when OAuth state is stored in the database and the server's time zone observes daylight saving time ([#12320](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12320))
- Fixed the OpenAPI schema to document query parameters for endpoints whose query schema is wrapped in `z.optional()`, such as `/get-session` and Stripe's `/subscription/list` ([#12337](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12337))
- Fixed `organization.getInvitation` to return the `INVITATION_NOT_FOUND` code for a missing, expired, or non-pending invitation ([#12332](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12332))
- Fixed `listMembers` failing with a syntax error on PostgreSQL and MSSQL when the filter matches no members or the offset is past the last member ([#12318](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12318))
- Fixed the `active-sessions` list in secondary storage being stored without an expiry when every remaining session had less than a second left ([#12323](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12323))
- Fixed SIWE sign-in leaving a user behind when creating its wallet address or account failed, which blocked that wallet from signing in again ([#12366](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12366))
- Fixed social sign-up hanging on single-connection databases when the username plugin is enabled and the provider profile maps a username ([#12340](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12340))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/5de71a89b1294564696dd3bc8161b2ff1ae9cdef/packages/better-auth/CHANGELOG.md)

## `auth`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed CLI commands hanging or exiting with code 0 at a prompt in CI or without a terminal. They now exit with code 2 and name what they need, such as `--yes`, and prompts appear on stderr so redirecting stdout no longer hides them ([#12286](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12286))
- Fixed CLI notices mixing into command output. `auth info --json --copy` now prints valid JSON, `auth secret` prints only the `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` line on stdout, `auth login` and `auth logout` messages go to stderr, and `auth info` shows tips only in an interactive terminal ([#12287](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12287))
- Fixed CLI errors printing a stack trace instead of the cause. Config and database errors now show their message, and a mistyped `--config` path reports that the file doesn't exist. `auth mcp` and `auth ai` no longer report success after a failed step ([#12305](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12305))
- Fixed the CLI exiting with code 0 after a canceled or failed run. Canceling or declining a prompt, or pressing Ctrl+C, now exits with 130, and failures such as a missing config file or a failed `auth mcp` setup exit with 1 ([#12275](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12275))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/5de71a89b1294564696dd3bc8161b2ff1ae9cdef/packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/oauth-provider`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed `auth.api.oauth2Consent({ headers, body })` failing with `request not found` when called from a server route ([#12325](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12325))
- Fixed a client secret without the configured `prefix.clientSecret` getting a different error than other wrong secrets. It now gets the standard `invalid_client` response: 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate: Basic` challenge for `client_secret_basic`, and 400 for `client_secret_post` ([#12327](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12327))
- Fixed OAuth client `metadata` being stored as a JSON string in its `json` column. It is now written as an object, so Postgres `jsonb` operators such as `->` and `@>` work with adapters that pass JSON through natively (Drizzle `pg`). Rows written as strings by earlier versions are still read ([#12328](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12328))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/5de71a89b1294564696dd3bc8161b2ff1ae9cdef/packages/oauth-provider/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/core`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed failed fallback join queries printing the raw database error, including SQL and bound values, with `console.error` in addition to the configured logger ([#12317](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12317))
- Fixed `getAccessToken` and `refreshToken` returning the expired access token when a provider refuses a token refresh with a 200 status, as GitHub does ([#12369](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12369))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/5de71a89b1294564696dd3bc8161b2ff1ae9cdef/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/expo`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed the Expo authorization proxy logging a provider configuration error on every OAuth sign-in when a social provider is set up for ID token sign-in only, such as Apple without a client secret ([#12368](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12368))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/5de71a89b1294564696dd3bc8161b2ff1ae9cdef/packages/expo/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/mcp`

### Bug Fixes

- Fixed MCP rejecting plain-HTTP `resource` URLs on `.localhost` subdomains as non-HTTPS ([#12322](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12322))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/5de71a89b1294564696dd3bc8161b2ff1ae9cdef/packages/mcp/CHANGELOG.md)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action required**
>
> - fix(oauth-provider)!: reject repeated parameters in form POST authorization requests ([#12261](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12261))
>
>   A form-encoded POST to `/oauth2/authorize` now follows the same repeated-parameter rules as a GET request. A standard parameter sent more than once, such as `state=a&state=b`, returns `invalid_request` with "state must not appear more than once". Before, the provider used the last value and could issue a code. A repeated `resource` now keeps every value instead of only the last one. A repeated custom parameter, such as `organization`, reaches `postLogin.consentReferenceId` and the signed `oauth_query` with every value. Clients that send each standard parameter once are unaffected.

- 5d18351: fix(ai): detect downloaded audio types from bytes when servers return a generic or non-audio content type such as application/octet-stream
- 8da48db: Respect `recordInputs` and `recordOutputs` when delivering telemetry events to integrations and the `ai:telemetry` channel. Filter nested content and omit raw span results when content recording is disabled, while preserving application results.
- fd7e8a7: Preserve the order of text and complete function calls in streamed Google responses, including standalone thought signatures on empty text or reasoning parts.

  Keep provider metadata on empty text parts when converting results to response messages so it can be passed back in subsequent requests.

  Omit foreign-provider empty signature text when replaying history through Anthropic or Bedrock, preserving Bedrock’s existing native reasoning-history handling.

- 36802d4: Support native URL transcription with an optional provider capability, keeping existing file-generation contracts unchanged. Groq sends HTTP(S) audio URLs through its `url` parameter without downloading and re-uploading them, avoiding the attachment upload limit. Supplying a custom `download` function retains local download behavior.

  For telemetry integrations, `TranscriptionEndEvent.audio.byteLength` and `audio.mediaType` can now be `undefined` when a provider fetches the audio URL natively. Check for missing values before using them as a number or string. Downloaded and inline audio continue to report their metadata; streaming transcription metadata is unchanged.

  Strip media fragments before sending URLs to Groq. If Groq rejects a redirect, fall back to the existing secure local downloader and file upload rather than failing previously working URL inputs. Other provider errors are preserved.

- 933dae3: fix (ai): download deprecated `file-url` and `image-url` tool result content

  Tool result content parts that use the deprecated `file-url` and `image-url`
  types were converted to `file` parts with `{ type: 'url' }` data, but they were
  never passed to the download function. When the model does not support the URL,
  the provider received a bare URL instead of the file contents, even though the
  replacement `file` part with `{ type: 'url' }` data was downloaded and inlined.

  Downloaded legacy URL parts now use the same media type normalization as file
  parts, resolving generic types from the response header or image bytes.
  Legacy base64 data URLs also normalize to inline data with the media type from
  their data URL, matching replacement file parts.

- e0143b0: feat(ai): support provider-owned realtime transports

  Add an optional `createTransport` interface and `provider` connection capability.

- 934100c: Report the actual OpenAI Chat HTTP endpoint (also used by Azure Chat and Bedrock Mantle Chat) through optional request metadata and model-call end events. Record its host and port on OpenTelemetry chat spans without exposing URL credentials, paths, queries, or fragments. Expose only the sanitized HTTP origin in text and object generation results and step/finish callbacks. Providers that do not report an endpoint leave these attributes unset.
- c389374: fix(ai): infer union output types when passing a union of schemas to `Output.object` and `Output.array`

  Previously, passing a schema whose type is a union of schemas (e.g. a schema selected from a map at runtime) failed to type-check because the output type was inferred from the first union member only. The output type is now inferred as the union of the schemas' output types.

- 892af4d: feat (ai): re-export realtime server-connection and usage types

  Adds `Experimental_RealtimeServerConnection`, `Experimental_RealtimeSessionIntent`, and `Experimental_RealtimeUsage` aliases for the new experimental `RealtimeModelV4` server-side spec types.

- 1a1da8d: stream steering messages to the ui and keep them in converted messages
- 41465fd: Expose optional transcription word timings separately from segments and accept shared timestampGranularities. Explicit provider timing settings take precedence. OpenAI now sends timestamp_granularities only with verbose_json and warns when a requested timing is unavailable or excluded.
- 9754014: Add typed streaming heartbeat parts. Anthropic emits them only with `includePings: true` (disabled by default), without requiring raw chunks. Core forwards pings through stream retries without storing them as generated content or sending them to UI message streams. Consumers with exhaustive stream-part switches must handle the new `ping` union variant when upgrading, even when the opt-in is disabled. Typed pings do not flush partial words during stream smoothing.
- 2e44144: Represent videos delivered directly to caller-managed storage with an explicit uploaded outcome. Video generation reports `uploadedVideos` without downloading or synthesizing video bytes; access `video` only when `videos` is nonempty.

- Fixed denying a device authorization request to reject a revoked session that is still in the cookie cache ([#12216](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12216))
- Fixed IP wildcard trusted origins such as `exp://192.168.*.*:*` matching custom-scheme hosts with out-of-range or zero-padded octets ([#12217](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12217))
- Fixed the phone number plugin storing an empty `phoneNumber` on sign-up and replacing a verified number when linking an account with an empty phone number ([#12219](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12219))
- Fixed TOTP verification rejecting API key sessions so they can now finish two-factor enrollment ([#12211](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12211))
- Fixed trusted devices being ignored when an app runs the two-factor sign-in step from its own hook on another sign-in path, such as email OTP ([#12228](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/12228))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/45909b9c3e84398b9c9b0749e46ba5563cb354f4/packages/better-auth/CHANGELOG.md)

releases.body:
## 📦 New builders: Bun, Rspack and Rsbuild

In addition to Rolldown, Rollup and Vite, Nitro can now build your server with three new **experimental** builders:

| Builder | Use it with |
| --- | --- |
| **Bun** ([#4987](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4987)) | `bun --bun nitro build` (selected automatically on Bun when `rolldown`/`vite` are not installed) |
| **Rspack** ([#4942](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4942)) | `builder: "rspack"` or `NITRO_BUILDER=rspack` |
| **Rsbuild** ([#5011](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5011)) | the `nitro()` plugin from `nitro/rsbuild` in `rsbuild.config.ts` |

All builders run the same Rollup-compatible plugins: Nitro's own, your [`buildPlugins`](https://nitro.build/config/build#buildplugins) and the ones presets add. So all Nitro features and deployment presets work with each builder.

### ⚡ Bun builder

```sh
bun --bun nitro build
```

The Bun builder bundles with `Bun.build`. It works with any preset (not only `bun`) and with `nitro dev`. Pass extra options with the new `bunConfig` option.

### 🦀 Rspack builder

```ts [nitro.config.ts]
export default defineConfig({ builder: "rspack" });
```

The Rspack builder bundles the server with [Rspack](https://rspack.rs) v2.3+. Like `rolldown` and `vite`, `@rspack/core` is installed on demand. It is not a dependency of Nitro. Load and transform filters become native Rspack loader conditions, so less work goes through JS. There is also a new `rspack` template for `nitro create`.

### 🧩 `nitro/rsbuild` plugin

```ts [rsbuild.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from "@rsbuild/core";
import { nitro } from "nitro/rsbuild";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [nitro()],
});
```

This plugin works like `nitro/vite`, using the environments API of [Rsbuild](https://rsbuild.rs). Client, SSR and the Nitro server compile in one Rsbuild compiler. `rsbuild dev`, `build`, `build --watch` and `preview` work with Nitro, as do SSR outlets in the HTML template, `?assets` imports and `services`. It also works with environments from other plugins, for example TanStack Start (`@tanstack/react-start/plugin/rsbuild`). 👉 [Rsbuild docs](https://nitro.build/docs/rsbuild) · examples: [`rsbuild-ssr-html`](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/tree/main/examples/rsbuild-ssr-html), [`rsbuild-ssr-react`](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/tree/main/examples/rsbuild-ssr-react), [`rsbuild-ssr-tss-react`](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/tree/main/examples/rsbuild-ssr-tss-react)

> [!NOTE]
> These builders are experimental: their behavior may change in minor releases. Known limits are listed in each PR. For example, `emitFile` only supports assets, and with Bun, library chunks are not grouped.

## 🔌 Shared `services` + `fetchService()` ([#5023](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5023))

Services are now part of Nitro core, with the same config and runtime API for `nitro/vite` and `nitro/rsbuild`:

```ts [nitro.config.ts]
export default defineConfig({
  services: { api: { entry: "./src/api-entry.ts" } },
});
```

```ts
import { fetchService } from "nitro/services";

const res = await fetchService("api", "/hello");
```

An `ssr` service is detected from an `entry-server` file. Your HTML template can render `<!--ssr-outlet-->` and use `fetchService` in its context. `vite.services` and `fetchViteEnv()` keep working as deprecated aliases.

## 🧱 Renderer templates compiled at build time ([#5019](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5019))

The renderer template is now compiled at build time, in dev and production, with all builders. Templates are no longer evaluated at runtime (`new Function`), so template syntax works in dev on workerd/Cloudflare too ([#5014](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5014)). Syntax errors name the template file. With Vite dev, page requests no longer wait for `transformIndexHtml` (~306 ms → ~3 ms per page request in a benchmark with a slow HTML plugin). This release also fixes `fetchViteEnv is not defined` during prerendering.

## ⚡ Vite integration

- **Built-in `?assets` imports** ([#5013](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5013)): `?assets` imports are now built into Nitro, based on the original work by Hiroshi Ogawa (@hi-ogawa). `nitro/rsbuild` supports them too.
- **Vite `base` ⇄ Nitro `baseURL`** ([#5022](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5022)): `vite build --base /app/` now serves routes and assets under `/app/`. Without a Vite `base`, Nitro `baseURL` is used as the Vite `base`. A `baseURL` set explicitly in Nitro config always wins.
- **Missing hashed assets return a `no-store` 404** ([#5020](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5020)): A request for an old chunk during a deploy no longer gets the HTML page with an immutable one-year cache header.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Behavior changes:** Server routes under the client `assetsDir` (`/assets/` by default) now return 404 in production builds. With only a Vite `base` set, dev now matches production. Set `baseURL: "/"` to keep the server at the root.

---

[compare changes](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/compare/v3.0.261102-rc...v3.0.261103-rc)

### 🚀 Enhancements

- Experimental `bun` builder ([#4987](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4987))
- Experimental `rspack` builder ([#4942](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4942))
- Shared `services` in core with `fetchService` from `nitro/services` ([#5023](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5023))
- Experimental `nitro/rsbuild` plugin ([#5011](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5011))

### 🩹 Fixes

- **dev:** Compile renderer template with workerd eval binding ([#5014](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5014))
- **vite:** Return `no-store` 404 for missing hashed client assets ([#5020](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5020))
- **vite:** Use vite `base` as nitro `baseURL` and vice versa ([#5022](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5022))

### 💅 Refactors

- **vite:** Built-in `?assets` imports ([#5013](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5013))
- Compile renderer template at build time in core ([#5019](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5019))

### 📖 Documentation

- Remove nightly-only mentions ([1d39bf2b](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/commit/1d39bf2b))

### Preset Changes

- **vercel:** Run scheduled tasks with vercel schedules (experimental) ([#4756](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/4756))
- **vercel:** Invoke path schedules with `GET` ([#5010](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/pull/5010))

- @TooTallNate
- @elliotdauber
- @pi0

releases.body:
> 4.6.4 is a security release. It fixes [eight advisories in Nuxt](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/security/advisories) and pulls in `nitropack` 2.13.6, which fixes [three more in Nitro](https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/security/advisories). We recommend upgrading as soon as you can.

## ⚠️ Behaviour changes

These probably won't affect most apps, but it's worth flagging anyway:

1. **Error details in production.** When a page fails to render on the server, the error page and the payload now only carry message and data of errors you create with `createError`. Everything else is stripped.
2. **Dev server `Host` checks.** Webpack and rspack dev servers now reject requests with an unexpected `Host` header, as Vite already does. If you use a custom hostname or tunnel, you'll need to add it to the new `devServer.allowedHosts` option.
3. **`workspaceDir` detection.** When `workspaceDir` isn't set, Nuxt now only widens it past `rootDir` to an explicit workspace root or the closest git repository. 
4. **Nitropack cached routes.** `cache`, `swr` and `isr` route rules now only cache `GET` and `HEAD` requests, and no longer store responses that set a cookie or send `Cache-Control: private` or `no-store`. Wildcard `proxy` and `redirect` rules also reject requests whose resolved target would leave the rule's scope.
5. **Route rules and encoded slashes.** Route rules now match paths that contain encoded slashes, so `/api%2Fadmin` is covered by a `/api/**` rule.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action required**
>
> OAuth profile types for Apple, Cognito, Discord, Dropbox, Facebook, GitHub, GitLab, Gumroad, Linear, Microsoft Entra ID, Notion, Patreon, PayPal, Railway, Slack, and Twitter(X) were reviewed against each provider's official resources and updated to match. If you use custom profile mappings or profile types for any of them, review the changes below and handle fields that are now optional, nullable, or retyped.

## `better-auth`

### ❗ Breaking Changes

- Fixed the Gumroad OAuth helper to return `undefined` for accounts without a name, matching its declared profile type ([#11864](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11864))
- Fixed the Patreon OAuth helper to normalize null names and images to missing values while preserving empty strings, and to allow email to be null or omitted when email access is not granted ([#11863](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11863))
- Fixed Slack sign-in to support scoped profiles with optional `SlackProfile` email and profile claims, use POST for userinfo in the built-in provider and Generic OAuth helper, and reject Slack errors returned with HTTP 200 ([#11851](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11851))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/f86eefd286c0bf4b24031255f0da359ab3cc9efc/packages/better-auth/CHANGELOG.md)

## `@better-auth/core`

### ❗ Breaking Changes

- Fixed Apple profile types to align with identity tokens, making private-email status, user status, and pictures optional and accepting boolean or string email-verification claims ([#11842](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11842))
- Fixed `CognitoProfile` to make profile and token claims optional, accept boolean or `"true"`/`"false"` verification values, fall back to `cognito:username` for ID-token names, and verify tokens against both documented issuer formats ([#11843](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11843))
- Fixed Discord profile types to reflect optional user metadata, added avatar decoration, collectible, and primary guild details, and defaulted missing email verification to false ([#11867](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11867))
- Fixed Dropbox profile types to include account status, locale, referral links, pairing status, account type, team policies, and root information, with `home_path` required for team roots ([#11846](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11846))
- Fixed Facebook Limited Login profile callbacks to accept tokens without name, email, or picture claims ([#11856](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11856))
- Fixed `GithubProfile` types to match GitHub API responses, with numeric `id` and account counters, nullable details, and omitted scope-dependent fields such as `twitter_username` ([#11839](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11839))
- Fixed GitLab profile handling for nullable details and omitted conditional fields, made `locked` a required boolean, and preserved stored images for null avatars when profile updates are enabled ([#11853](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11853))
- Fixed `LinearUser.avatarUrl` to be required and typed as `string | null`, preserved stored images for null avatars during enabled profile updates, and made authorization scopes comma-separated ([#11855](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11855))
- Fixed `MicrosoftEntraIDProfile` claim types so timestamps are numbers, `groups`, `acrs`, and `xms_cc` are string arrays, `in_corp` is boolean, and conditional claims and profile photos can be omitted ([#11854](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11854))
- Fixed Notion users without an avatar to keep their existing profile image when profile updates are enabled, with optional `type`, nullable `name` and `avatar_url`, missing `image` as `undefined`, and optional `person.email_verified` metadata ([#11859](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11859))
- Fixed PayPal profile types to handle omitted names, email, and verification claims when personal permissions are not granted, defaulting missing email verification to false ([#11862](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11862))
- Fixed `RailwayProfile` to make `email`, `name`, and `picture` optional, reflecting the granted scopes ([#11861](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11861))
- Fixed Slack sign-in to support scoped profiles with optional `SlackProfile` email and profile claims, use POST for userinfo in the built-in provider and Generic OAuth helper, and reject Slack errors returned with HTTP 200 ([#11851](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11851))
- Fixed `TwitterProfile` types so nested entity objects, arrays, and URL details can be omitted or `null`, and added description cashtags, mentions, and URL preview metadata ([#11852](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/11852))

For detailed changes, see [`CHANGELOG`](https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/f86eefd286c0bf4b24031255f0da359ab3cc9efc/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md)

### Patch Changes

- 8e18d59: feat(ai): add experimental_streamSpeech

  Streams speech audio from a string, or an array, iterable, or stream of text deltas and/or text parts (each with an optional `voice` and `providerOptions`) using speech models that implement the experimental `Experimental_StreamingSpeechModelV4` extension. Returns a single-consumer `audioStream` / `fullStream` plus `usage`, `warnings`, `responses`, and `providerMetadata` promises. Provider `error` parts are non-fatal and reported through `onError` (default `console.error`). A user abort or a cancel rejects the result promises immediately. Exports the `Experimental_SpeechTextPart`, `Experimental_SpeechStreamPart`, `Experimental_SpeechStreamUsage`, and `Experimental_StreamSpeechResult` types, adds an optional `cause` to `NoSpeechGeneratedError`, and adds `Experimental_MockStreamingSpeechModelV4` to `ai/test`.

releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- 1727442: fix(ai): process only the first approval response per tool call, so repeated or conflicting responses in the final tool message no longer execute a tool twice or both execute and deny it
- 0a5d0e7: Fix `toolChoice: 'none'` by forwarding it to the Hugging Face Responses API and rejecting tool calls before local execution in `generateText`, `streamText`, and `WorkflowAgent`. Streamed tool parts are withheld so client-side tools cannot act on them, and `repairToolCall` and `experimental_refineToolInput` are not invoked for rejected tool calls.
- 10026d1: Add the `interrupted` finish reason for provider streams that end without a completion signal. Preserve partial output without introducing an error solely for interruption, and stop tool execution, agent continuation, and automatic UI follow-ups for interrupted responses, including late tool results and approvals. Provider detection and emission will be added separately.

  **Compatibility notice:** Adding `interrupted` to the public finish-reason types can break type checking after upgrading, even though this is a patch release. Exhaustive switches (for example, using an `assertNever` fallback) and mappings such as `Record<FinishReason, string>` must handle the new value. Update any custom validation or application logic that assumes the existing set of finish reasons is exhaustive.

  When providers begin emitting `interrupted`, a stream ending without a completion signal will preserve partial output and report this finish reason without emitting an error solely for the interruption. Applications that need to detect incomplete responses should check `finishReason === 'interrupted'` as well as their existing error handling.
